title: Breakdown of Net Investment Returns and Net Investment Income Components in Contributions to Government Budgets
what_it_is: Breakdown of Net Investment Returns and Net Investment Income Components in Contributions to Government Budgets

sections.label: NIRC share of Budget
sections.summary: Asks what percentage of Net Investment Returns and Net Investment Income contributed to the Budget over five years and this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) for each year in the last five financial years, what is the percentage of the Net Investment Returns (NIR) and the Net Investment Income (NII) that contributed to the Government's Budget as Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC); and (b) what is the estimated percentage of the NIR and the NII to be contributed to the Government's Budget as NIRC for this financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We plan to take in the maximum 50% of NII and NIR for FY2021, in view of the expected overall Budget deficit.

sections.label: NIRC amount and components
sections.summary: States the NIRC dollar amount depends on the smoothened net asset base and expected long-term return rate, with FY2021 breakdown unavailable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The absolute dollar amount that we get from NIRC will be both a function of the smoothened net asset base as well as the expected long-term rate of return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As to the components which contribute to the FY2021 figures, I do not think we have the breakdown today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because there would be a process based on what the smoothened base is and then, what the expected long-term rate of return is, and there are processes in place, as we have described in this House, to ascertain each of these figures which then are submitted to the President's Office for the President's approval.
